title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: approve or reject — the only tests of a review decision
content:
## Rule
Under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product a review is decided only once every condition for deciding it holds; while any such condition is missing, the review stays under review and no decision is recorded. A review that can be decided is decided as approved when the goods fit the category and as rejected otherwise. The goods fit the category only when every test of fit applied at the decision holds on the acceptance as it stands at the decision; a single failed test means they do not fit. These tests of fit are the only tests of the decision. The booking mix and the sailing allotment are admission conditions, counted when an application or an amendment is admitted, and the decision does not count them again. Likewise the applicant conditions of admission — contract rating, customer tenure, the misdeclaration block, the resubmission wait and the limited-quantity routing — are tested when the application is admitted and not again at the decision.

## Order of judgement
1. Can the review be decided? If a condition for deciding it is missing: no decision; the acceptance stays under review.
2. If it can be decided: do the goods fit on every test of fit? Yes: approved. No: rejected.

## What is not re-tested at the decision
| Matter | Tested at the decision |
|---|---|
| booking mix on the booking | no — admission condition |
| per-shipper sailing allotment | no — admission condition |
| contract rating of the booking | no — tested at admission |
| customer tenure | no — tested at admission |
| misdeclaration block | no — tested at admission |
| waiting period after a rejection | no — tested at admission |
| limited-quantity routing | no — tested at admission |

## Wrong reading and correct basis
- *Wrong*: "The sailing now holds more of the customer's containers than the allotment, so the review must be rejected." *Correct*: the allotment is counted when an application or amendment is admitted; the decision does not count it again, and the review is approved if the goods fit.
- *Wrong*: "The goods fit, but a condition for deciding is still missing, so approve anyway." *Correct*: while any condition for deciding is missing, no decision is recorded.
- *Wrong*: "One test of fit fails, but most pass, so approve." *Correct*: the goods fit only when every test holds; otherwise the review is rejected.
